text:
lucy: Heads up - bringing up model-y:int8 I hit a weird repeating tail on long-prefill runs (>16k primer). Float32/FP16 baseline clean.
omar: Can you show a tiny repro and the diffs?
lucy: Repro steps:
1) git checkout release/quant-int8/model-y
2) ./eval_long --model staging/model-y:int8 --prompt-file tests/long_prompts/merchant_journey.txt --max-tokens 4096 --prefill=true
3) compare to staging/model-y:fp16
Diff snippet (trimmed):
```
-- fp16: "...they rounded the corner and found the lantern still lit, a single ember keeping watch like memory."
++ int8: "...they rounded the corner and found the lantern still lit, a single ember keeping watch like memory. they rounded the corner and found the lantern still lit..."
```
Basically the tail repeats a 9-12 token span, not a typical off-by-one. Happens only with warm prefill, cold starts fine.
kasia: Hmm, sounds like KV alignment / evict window bug. Any changes in the packer that touch offsets or stride?
lucy: The quant packer added an optimization to compress per-shard offsets into uint32 for space. I found this in packer/offsets.py:
```
# offsets.py
class OffsetTable:
    def add(self, shard_id, offset):
        # store as uint32 in on-disk index
        self.table[shard_id] = np.uint32(offset)
```
Offsets can exceed 4B when seq_len*layer_count*kv_entry > 4e9 for very long primers + many layers.
rahul: Ah, uint32 wrap would cause the prefill to write into the wrong slot and later reads return stale KV, which could cause repeating segments. Any quick patch?
lucy: I monkeypatched to use np.uint64 and re-ran the same prompt under int8 - repeating tail disappeared. Outputs match fp16 semantic flow for the whole 20k window.
omar: Nice find. We should backport a hotfix for staging packs and add a failing integration test.
kasia: Also add a cross-check in the runtime that validates prefill index monotonicity and emits a warning if we would wrap. Easier to catch in prod.
lucy: I'll open PR that: 1) changes offsets to uint64 in packer; 2) adds an integration test with primer lengths [8k,16k,24k] and asserts no trailing repeats (edit distance threshold) after prefill; 3) runtime assert on index wrap. PR: https://git.redwood/modely/pull/512
ci-bot: perf-regression #5021: model-y:int8 latency -7% vs fp16; artifacts uploaded -> https://ci.redwood/artifacts/5021
rahul: For completeness, run a parity check where we dump KV entries after prefill and compare the fingerprints between fp16 and int8 for the same primer. That will catch misaligned writes even if outputs occasionally converge.
lucy: Good call. I added a small KV-dump comparator to the PR tests. Also adding a fuzz harness that randomizes shard sizes and prefix lengths to catch wrapping cases.
omar: Should we consider adding compile-time guards in the packer that error if expected max offset > 2**32? Safer than silent wrap.
kasia: Yes make it fail-fast - better than subtle corruption in long-context workloads.
lucy: Will do. Tagging this P1 for staging. Will hold int8 rollout until PR merges and long-context bench passes.
omar: Great work. Thanks for the quick bisect. :pray:
